extraction.Name: John Garnier
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 640 acre allotment at the time it was issued, because he did not wish to pay taxes on it, but was told by the Indian Agency, that it would be taxed at any rate, and be sold for these taxes, if he did not take care of it, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged half of the allotment to De Moulin Loan And Investment Company, of Hot Springs, South Dakota, for $500.00 (receiving $410.83 after loan charges deducted); sold the whole section to Edwin G. Fowler, of Oelrichs, South Dakota for assuming the mortgage and paying $400.00 besides ($50.00 upon date of sale and $350.00 within ten days after the sale)
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: sold it on account of having a sick wife; was told by the Indian Agency that it would be taxed at any rate, and be sold for these taxes, if he did not take care of it
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms his wife's land, and, sometimes in the fall, he goes out in the potato fields of Nebraska, for three or four weeks to work; and that this is his only income
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent, has good health; wife has very poor health, having chronic appendicitis; three boys to support, all of whom have good health; used mortgage proceeds for improvements on wife's place; considers he got an extra poor price for his land; sold on November 6, 1920; mortgaged June 26, 1920; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; affidavit sworn November 27, 1928
